summary: Streaming client heartbeats prolong continuous-batcher linger window causing p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent 504s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (LinguaFlow) reports repeated p95/p99 latency spikes and intermittent 504s on short inference requests coming from streaming clients. Problem first observed after a traffic pattern change on 2026-03-11 where many short streaming sessions (heartbeat every 2s) were introduced.

Impact:
- Several endpoints for LinguaFlow saw 2–5x increase in p99 request latency during peak; intermittent 504s for short generate calls (< 30 tokens).
- Affects dedicated capacity pool in us-west; downstream SLAs at risk for enterprise contract.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: prod-us-west (tenant: lingualow-dedicated)
- Model: redwood-infer-1 pinned to v2026-02-28
- Traffic: mixed streaming and non-streaming; short requests (< 30 tokens) predominant in new client release

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Open ~150 concurrent streaming connections from client that sends periodic heartbeat frames every 1–3s but only occasionally submits short generate requests.
2) Submit a burst of short single-shot generate requests interleaved with heartbeats from some connections.
3) Observe p95/p99 spike and occasional 504s for short requests; longer requests (> 100 tokens) largely unaffected.

Observed metrics and logs:
- Continuous-batcher flush interval increased from expected 10–25ms to 120–400ms for affected slots (trace sampling).
- Token throughput remained within capacity; GPU utilization ~60–75%.
- Trace spans show batcher linger reset events triggered by streaming keepalive frames.
- Router logs: increased queuing time at batcher ingress for short requests (~80–350ms added).
- Error logs: intermittent upstream 504s with 'batcher-timeout' marker.

Immediate customer impact: degraded latency for interactive features (autosuggest/autocomplete) used within LinguaFlow editor. Customer requested a high-priority mitigation and postmortem.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Spin up a subset of the dedicated pool in us-west with model redwood-infer-1 pinned. 2) Launch ~150 streaming clients that maintain open streams and send heartbeat frames every 1–3s. 3) Interleave short generation requests (<30 tokens) from a subset of clients. 4) Observe p95/p99 latency and occasional 504s in router/batcher metrics.

investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis (Support): batcher was accumulating short requests because streaming heartbeats were being treated as request activity and kept linger window open.
- Collected traces from affected tenant and sampled batcher metrics during spike windows.
- Found correlation between number of active streaming connections sending heartbeats and batcher linger durations rising. Heartbeat frames are processed by streaming-proxy and create a 'recent_activity' touch on connection which the batcher uses to decide linger resetting.
- SRE reproduced locally by replaying heartbeat-only traffic and observed linger amplification: frequent tiny frames prevented batcher from closing earlier leading to head-of-line blocking for incoming short requests that did not belong to the same microbatch.
- Related INT-480 documented prior fix to ignore websocket ping frames for linger; however the customer's client implements heartbeat as an application-level empty payload that our proxy treats differently.
- No GPUs OOM or scheduler failures; behavior purely at queuing/latency level within serving runtime's continuous-batcher logic.
root_cause: Continuous-batcher linger semantics treat application-level streaming heartbeats as activity and extend the per-slot linger window, causing sustained linger amplification under high numbers of idle streaming connections. This leads to larger microbatches or delayed flushes and head-of-line blocking of short, latency-sensitive requests. The proxy's classification of heartbeats differs from websocket pings and bypasses previous ignore-rules.
resolution:
Mitigation (applied 2026-03-13 21:30 UTC to prod-us-west for LinguaFlow tenant):
- Short-term: updated streaming-proxy config to classify empty payload heartbeats as 'keepalive' and not surface them as activity to the continuous-batcher. Deploy rolled to 3/3 nodes in dedicated pool.
- Short-term #2: lowered batcher linger upper cap for dedicated pools to 60ms for short-request lanes to reduce worst-case hold time for latency-sensitive traffic.
- Monitoring: synthetic short-request test added to tenant smoke tests; alert threshold added for batcher linger > 100ms.

Status: Customer reports significant improvement in p95/p99 post-mitigation during smoke windows; no more 504s observed in sampled windows. Changes remain in canary for 24–48h before org-wide rollout.
rollout_notes:
- 2026-03-13 20:50 UTC: created canary config with updated streaming-proxy classification.
- 2026-03-13 21:10 UTC: canary deploy to 1 node, smoke tests passed.
- 2026-03-13 21:30 UTC: config rolled to remaining nodes for LinguaFlow dedicated pool.
- 2026-03-14 09:00 UTC: expanded monitoring and set PagerDuty alert for linger > 120ms.
